Consult Summary:
- Teleconsultation for acute respiratory symptoms with fever and hemoptysis in a 45-year-old woman with SLE on methotrexate; suspected chest infection; plan for same-day in-person chest assessment and potential antibiotics and imaging.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Shortness of breath with right-sided back pain on deep inspiration; fever; hemoptysis on two occasions; fatigue and reduced ability to exercise.
- Onset/duration/progression: Symptoms notable today for dyspnea and pleuritic pain; tiredness for about 2 weeks; cough with blood occurred yesterday and again today.
- Associated symptoms: Feels heart racing at times.
- Negative findings: Non-smoker; no long-haul flights; no known DVT; no cancer history beyond SLE.
- Past medical history: SLE.
- Medications: Methotrexate (for SLE); last dose this morning; dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Allergies: None documented.
- Social history: Lives alone (flat); works a desk job; has a cat.

Examination:
- Vitals: Pulse checked; estimated heart rate about 66–74 bpm. No other vitals recorded.
- Exam findings: Capillary refill described as very good (normal circulation). Throat exam performed with patient able to say "ah" (no abnormal finding noted). Neck: no enlarged glands. Patient not described as acutely unstable.

Impression:
- Working diagnosis: Chest infection suspected; pneumonia considered as a differential. Lung cancer unlikely based on current presentation, but investigations may be needed to exclude it.

Plan:
- Immediate plan: Arrange an in-person clinic review today with chest auscultation, blood pressure check, pulse recheck, and temperature measurement.
- Management considerations: May require an antibiotic if chest infection confirmed; no antibiotic prescribed today pending formal assessment.
- Investigations: Consider chest X-ray if symptoms do not settle or to further evaluate pneumonia vs other pathology.
- Follow-up: Support team to book a same-day face-to-face appointment with a GP; note left in appointment for patient to contact support.
- Allergies to antibiotics: None documented.

Quality checks:
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - Allergies to medications documented as none, but explicit med reconciliation findings (e.g., full list of current meds) beyond methotrexate not provided.
  - Specific vital signs (blood pressure, temperature, respiratory rate, oxygen saturation) not recorded.
  - Antibiotic dosing details not documented since antibiotics were not prescribed yet.
- Internal conflicts:
  - Name inconsistency: patient identified as Tracy Chapman earlier, then referred to as Doris later in the conversation.
- Transcript quality:
  - Some conversational repetition and informal phrasing; overall sufficient to identify presenting symptoms and planned actions.
